body:
[aida:product] STORY-1422 criterion 2 BLOCKED on a measurement that invalidates my own design choice. The gate does not trip on the real store, and it is right not to — by a rule that is wrong for this data.

I BUILT IT, RAN IT AGAINST THE REAL STORE WITH A 1000 ms BUDGET, AND IT EXITED 0. Rather than adjust until it went red, I measured the population it judges.

    `show` events in ~/.aida/usage.jsonl        23,112
    median all-time                                404 ms
    median last 7d / 24h / 6h / 1h        664 / 667 / 663 / 665 ms
    p90     last 7d / 24h / 6h / 1h     5821 / 9653 / 1138 /  812 ms
    over 1000 ms                           18-21% depending on window

THE DISTRIBUTION IS BIMODAL, NOT NOISY. In the last 24h: 4,777 calls at or under 5 s and 794 above it, with the slow group clustered near 9.9 s. It is not a fast population with outliers; it is two populations sharing a command name.

SO MY STATISTIC IS WRONG, AND I WANT TO BE PRECISE ABOUT HOW. I chose the MEDIAN and defended it to you: one slow sample is a loaded machine, a gate that trips on noise gets its budget raised. I wrote a test pinning it — a single 9.9 s sample among fast ones must not trip — and I MUTATED that test to prove it fires. The test is internally valid and the mutation was real. The decision it pins is wrong for this population, because the reasoning assumed unimodal noise and the data is bimodal. A correct test can pin a wrong decision; that is a failure mode I had not hit before tonight.

NONE OF THE THREE OBVIOUS STATISTICS WORKS:
    median          404-667 ms — never trips, including right now with the bug live
    p90             812 ms to 9653 ms across windows — unstable, would flap
    any-over-budget 18-21% of calls — always trips, including after a fix

THE ONE THAT DOES FIT THE DATA is a PROPORTION over a recent window: trip when more than X% of a shape's calls exceed its budget. Measured: 20% in the last 24h, 7% in the last hour, and after BUG-1480's fix the slow mode should approach zero because the slow mode IS the bug. A proportion is stable across windows in a way p90 is not, it is interpretable to a human reading a ledger entry, and it matches the acceptance criterion's own sense — "completes in under one second" as the normal case, not the best case.

THIS CHANGES THE SEMANTICS YOU RULED, so I am not implementing it unasked. The spec says "EXITS NON-ZERO when a command shape exceeds its budget". A proportion gate says "exits non-zero when a shape exceeds its budget TOO OFTEN", which needs a second number — the tolerated fraction — and that number is policy, not a constant I should pick alone.

ONE MORE THING THE DATA SAYS, and it is uncomfortable for the instrument generally: the fast and slow groups are INDISTINGUISHABLE by every field the log records — role, scope, binary_sha, args_count, exit_code all have the same shape in both. The log deliberately stores no argument values (the STORY-122 privacy floor), so nothing recorded explains why the same command against the same binary takes 400 ms or 9,900 ms. Whatever separates them is invisible to the instrument that is supposed to guard it. That is worth knowing before anyone leans on this gate as the only guard.

WHAT I HAVE THAT IS DONE AND VERIFIED: config reader, breach detection, unobserved-budget findings, the opt-in --fail-on-findings gate, the category registered, the substrate job plus a CronJobFailed-keyed routing seat job scaffolded, six tests green with all six mutations confirmed red.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU: the statistic and, if it is a proportion, the tolerated fraction. I would propose 5% over a 24h window on the measured numbers, but I would rather you set it than inherit mine.
subject: STORY-1422 blocked: the show-latency distribution is BIMODAL — median never trips, p90 flaps 812-9653ms, any-over-budget always trips. My median choice is measurably wrong
